partial_progress.details: Phase 7 of 11 (Gate-Level Concurrency Scheduler) complete and committed cleanly. Added a new gate_registry_exec_concurrent_batch worker-slot-pool scheduler to lib/gate-registry-lib.sh (ported in shape from run-all.sh's own proven pool), a new --jobs N|auto flag on verify-deploy.sh (default auto, nproc capped at 4; --jobs 1 is the byte-identical sequential opt-out), wave-barrier dependency honouring, serialized-class isolation for gate 8, longest-first cost-class scheduling, and a VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED nested-invocation guard mirroring RUN_ALL_NESTED. Two real concurrency bugs were caught and fixed via this phase's own new test coverage: (1) a naive sequential state-dump sourcing that silently drops every concurrently-forked gate's contribution except the last, fixed with a snapshot-once-per-group/apply-delta-per-id reconciliation design; (2) an intermittent (~1-in-10) worker-cap violation caused by a mapfile/process-substitution pipeline's own background reader occasionally being reaped by the dispatch loop's first `wait -n` instead of a real pool job, fixed with a bare `wait` draining the pipeline before the dispatch loop begins. Output and the final PASS/FAIL line are proven byte-identical across worker counts on both synthetic registries (library-level tests) and the real 23-gate registry. A full, unscoped verify-deploy.sh --findings run (auto jobs, load ~4-6/24) completed in 790s (13.2 min) with a finding set matching Phase 6's documented baseline exactly (Gate 8's 5-suite failure set identical; Gate 20's eager-load finding exactly 988B over baseline matching the dispatch's own named exclusion; Gate 3/5's content-drift findings for this phase's own touched files are expected, already-documented pre-redeploy accumulation deferred to Phase 11, not a regression; Gate 4/16 findings confirmed unrelated). Measured real speedup: a 7-gate moderate-cost selection went from ~70s (jobs=1) to ~43s (jobs=4). Pausing at this clean phase boundary; Phase 8 (one-process-per-file shellcheck parallelization) depends only on Phase 3 and can start cleanly.

completion_data.completion_summary: Completed phase 7 of the 11-phase gate-framework refactor: added gate-level concurrency to verify-deploy.sh via a new --jobs N|auto flag and a worker-slot-pool scheduler (gate_registry_exec_concurrent_batch) ported from run-all.sh's own proven shape, with wave-barrier dependency honouring, serialized-class isolation, longest-first scheduling, and a nested-invocation guard. Caught and fixed two real concurrency bugs during implementation (a state-reconciliation data-loss bug and an intermittent worker-cap violation) via dedicated new test coverage (21 and 18 cases respectively in the two touched test suites). Proved output determinism across worker counts and measured a real ~1.6x speedup on a representative gate subset, with a full unscoped battery run matching Phase 6's documented baseline finding set. Phases 8-11 (shellcheck parallelization, corpus enumeration, run-all.sh default flip, final redeploy and measured verification) remain.

memory_candidates.content: A bash function that mutates caller-scope globals (CHECKS, FAILURES, an array, etc.) across a REAL forked subshell (needed for a killable timeout) via a declare -p dump/source roundtrip works correctly for ONE sequential caller, but breaks silently under CONCURRENCY: every concurrently-forked subshell inherits the SAME baseline snapshot of the globals and dumps 'baseline + its own delta', not a running total. A caller that naively does `source state.$id` for each id in sequence REPLACES the globals with each id's own baseline-relative value instead of ACCUMULATING them, silently dropping every id's contribution except the last one sourced. Fix: snapshot the real vars' baseline ONCE per concurrently-dispatched group (array length for arrays, numeric value for scalars), then for each id's dump compute and APPLY only that id's own delta (sum for a numeric scalar, append-only-the-new-tail-elements for an array, last-write-wins for a non-numeric scalar) against the shared snapshot.

A bash function that resets a GLOBAL associative array (declare -gA MAP=()) via a bare `MAP=()` reassignment is unsafe if ANYTHING else in the program `unset`s that same variable between calls: `unset` on a `declare -gA` variable destroys its TYPE along with its value, so a later bare `MAP=()` silently recreates it as an ORDINARY INDEXED array instead of associative. A subsequent string-keyed assignment (`MAP["somename"]=val`) on an indexed array evaluates the key ARITHMETICALLY, and if the real variable the key names already holds a hyphenated element value (e.g. an array element 'finding-1'), bash's arithmetic evaluator parses that as a SUBTRACTION expression and chokes on the unset bare identifier before the hyphen -- producing a crash ('X: unbound variable') that looks completely unrelated to the real defect. Fix: always reassert `declare -gA MAP=()` (not a bare `MAP=()`) on every reset of a global associative array whose lifetime spans multiple calls with an `unset` between them.

A bash worker-slot-pool scheduler shaped like `mapfile -t ARR < <(pipeline) ; for id in ARR; do while active>=cap; do wait -n; active--; done; job & active++; done` has a subtle, intermittent (~1-in-10 to 1-in-15) cap-violation bug: the `mapfile < <(pipeline)` process substitution backgrounds its OWN reader process to feed the substitution, and that reader can still be unwaited in bash's job table when the dispatch loop's FIRST `wait -n` call runs. That first `wait -n` can reap the leftover pipeline reader instead of one of the loop's own backgrounded jobs, decrementing the active-worker counter with no real job having finished, letting one EXTRA job launch past the declared cap. Fix: add a bare `wait` immediately after the mapfile/pipeline line and before the dispatch loop begins, to drain the pipeline's own reader first. A naive, non-atomic read-modify-write counter used to TEST for cap violations can only ever UNDER-count a real violation (never fabricate one), so it can mask this bug for many runs; use a `flock`-guarded atomic counter, or real start/end timestamp overlap checking, to reliably detect it.
